title: The Gross Amount Coming Back on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Given Up
content:
The gross amount coming back on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass is taken as follows.

**First.** Where the tier's refund basis is the pro rata basis and the pass account shows at least one lift scan entry, the gross amount is the price committed to multiplied by the share of the season still to come, with no day use deduction taken.

**Second.** Where the tier's refund basis is the pro rata basis and the pass account shows no lift scan entry at all, the gross amount is the price committed to in full.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the gross amount is not taken differently by this rule.

### The two conditions

| The tier's refund basis | Lift scan entries on the pass account | The gross amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the pro rata basis | at least one | the price committed to multiplied by the share of the season still to come, no day use deduction taken |
| the pro rata basis | none at all | the price committed to in full |
| the day use basis | any | not taken differently by this rule |

Both conditions rest on the refund basis published for the tier: only a tier whose basis is the pro rata basis reaches either of them, and on a tier whose basis is the day use basis neither condition is met however the scan entries stand.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A Granite Ridge Collective Unlimited Pass, whose refund basis is the pro rata basis, committed to 1879.00, with a share of the season still to come of 60 set against 100.

Where the pass account shows three lift scan entries, the gross amount is 1879.00 multiplied by that share, which is 1127.40, and no day use deduction is taken from it. Where it shows no lift scan entry at all, the gross amount is the price committed to in full, 1879.00. The figure this rule produces is carried as it stands and is not rounded at this step.
